requirements.text: The representative ESA (rear combination lamp with its LED modules, PCB, wiring and connector) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 6 of this Regulation (emissions and immunity in configurations other than REESS charging mode) for ESA type approval to be granted; paragraph 7 does not apply because the lamp is not used in REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid.
requirements.test_case: Review the test reports for radiated and conducted emission and immunity tests (paras 6.5, 6.6, 6.8, Annex 10) and confirm that all results meet paragraph 6.

requirements.text: Since the ESA is (part of) a light source, the ESA shall have the documentation specified in paragraph 3.2.10; without it, approval of the ESA under Regulation No. 10 shall not be granted.
requirements.test_case: Check that the approval file contains either an R37/R99/R128 approval number or a Technical Service non-interchangeability report for the LED light source.

requirements.text: In case of non-replaceable LED modules, a test report by a designated Technical Service shall be provided stating that the LED module/ESA is not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, No. 99 or No. 128.
requirements.test_case: Have the Technical Service inspect the LED module interface and compare it with the R37/R99/R128 light source caps, then issue the report.

requirements.text: In case of a replaceable LED light source approved under Regulation No. 128, the approval number granted to this light source under Regulation No. 128 shall be specified for the ESA.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the R128 approval number is quoted in the application and matches the marking on the light source.

requirements.text: An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every ESA (rear lamp) conforming to a type approved under UN R10.
requirements.test_case: Inspect production samples of the rear lamp for the presence of the R10 approval mark.

requirements.text: The international approval mark shall be affixed in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form.
requirements.test_case: Compare the mark location on the lamp with the location stated on the approval communication form.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the mark for the circled "E" and the correct country number.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall comprise the number of this Regulation (10), followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number, placed to the right of the circle.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the mark for "10R-" followed by the approval number to the right of the circle.

requirements.text: The approval markings on the ESA may be located so that they are not visible when the ESA (rear lamp) is installed in the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Check that the mark is present on the lamp (e.g. on the housing rear side), even if it is hidden after installation.

requirements.text: The ESA (rear combination lamp with LED modules and drive electronics) shall be designed, constructed and fitted so that the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, can comply with the requirements of UN R10.
requirements.test_case: Design review of the lamp's EMC design, followed by completion of all applicable ESA EMC tests.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
requirements.test_case: Check that the test plan and test reports cover radiated emission, conducted transient emission, radiated immunity and conducted transient immunity.

requirements.text: The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.
requirements.test_case: Perform an Annex 7 broadband radiated emission measurement on the lamp in normal operation (all lamp functions on).

requirements.text: When measured according to Annex 7, the ESA broadband radiated emission limit shall be: 62 to 52 dBµV/m in the 30–75 MHz band, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz; 52 to 63 dBµV/m in the 75–400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz; and a constant 63 dBµV/m in the 400–1,000 MHz band (Appendix 6).
requirements.test_case: Compare Annex 7 quasi-peak readings from 30 to 75 MHz with the log-decreasing limit line of Appendix 6.

requirements.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband emission values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type-approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Verify that all broadband readings lie below the limit line across 30 to 1,000 MHz.

requirements.text: The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.
requirements.test_case: Perform an Annex 8 narrowband radiated emission measurement on the lamp in normal operation.

requirements.text: When measured according to Annex 8, the ESA narrowband radiated emission limit shall be: 52 to 42 dBµV/m in the 30–75 MHz band, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz; 42 to 53 dBµV/m in the 75–400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz; and a constant 53 dBµV/m in the 400–1,000 MHz band (Appendix 7).
requirements.test_case: Compare Annex 8 average-detector readings from 30 to 75 MHz with the Appendix 7 limit line.

requirements.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband emission value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type-approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Verify that all narrowband readings lie below the limit line across 30 to 1,000 MHz.

requirements.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances by the ESA on its 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 7637-2, as described in Annex 10, against the maximum pulse amplitudes of Table 1.
requirements.test_case: Perform an ISO 7637-2 transient emission measurement on the lamp supply line while the functions are switched on and off.

requirements.text: For an ESA for vehicles with 12 V systems, the transient conducted emission on the supply lines shall not exceed a positive pulse amplitude of +75 V or a negative pulse amplitude of -100 V.
requirements.test_case: Record the maximum positive pulse amplitude per ISO 7637-2 and compare it with +75 V.

requirements.text: For an ESA for vehicles with 24 V systems, the transient conducted emission on the supply lines shall not exceed a positive pulse amplitude of +150 V or a negative pulse amplitude of -450 V.
requirements.test_case: Record the maximum positive pulse amplitude per ISO 7637-2 and compare it with +150 V.

requirements.text: The immunity of the ESA representative of its type to electromagnetic radiation shall be tested by one or more methods chosen from those described in Annex 9 (absorber chamber/ALSE, TEM cell, BCI, stripline, reverberation chamber).
requirements.test_case: Perform a radiated immunity test on the lamp per Annex 9 using the selected method(s).

requirements.text: If the stripline method is used, the radiated immunity test level shall be 60 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: Stripline test from 20 to 400 MHz at 60 V/m, confirming coverage of at least 90 % of the band.

requirements.text: If the TEM cell method is used, the radiated immunity test level shall be 75 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 200 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: TEM cell test from 20 to 200 MHz at 75 V/m.

requirements.text: If the BCI method is used, the immunity test level shall be 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: BCI test on the lamp harness from 20 to 400 MHz at 60 mA.

requirements.text: If the ALSE method is used, the radiated immunity test level shall be 30 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 80 to 2,000 MHz band and 10 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: ALSE test at 30 V/m (80 to 2,000 MHz) and 10 V/m (2 to 6 GHz).

requirements.text: If the reverberation chamber method is used, the radiated immunity test level shall be 21 V/m in over 90 per cent of the LUF to 2,000 MHz band and 7 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: Reverberation chamber test at 21 V/m (LUF to 2 GHz) and 7 V/m (2 to 6 GHz).

requirements.text: If the stripline method is used, the minimum radiated immunity test level over the whole 20 to 400 MHz band shall be 50 V/m.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the stripline field never falls below 50 V/m from 20 to 400 MHz.

requirements.text: If the TEM cell method is used, the minimum radiated immunity test level over the whole 20 to 200 MHz band shall be 62.5 V/m.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the TEM cell field never falls below 62.5 V/m from 20 to 200 MHz.

requirements.text: If the BCI method is used, the minimum immunity test level over the whole 20 to 400 MHz band shall be 50 mA.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the injected current never falls below 50 mA from 20 to 400 MHz.

requirements.text: If the ALSE method is used, the minimum radiated immunity test level shall be 25 V/m over the whole 80 to 2,000 MHz band and 8 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the ALSE field is at least 25 V/m (80 to 2,000 MHz) and 8 V/m (2 to 6 GHz) at all frequencies.

requirements.text: If the reverberation chamber method is used, the minimum radiated immunity test level shall be 18 V/m over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz band and 6 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the reverberation chamber field is at least 18 V/m (LUF to 2 GHz) and 6 V/m (2 to 6 GHz).

requirements.text: During the radiated immunity tests according to Annex 9, there shall be no degradation of performance of the immunity-related functions of the ESA (stop lamp and rear position lamp).
requirements.test_case: Monitor the stop lamp and rear position lamp light output (e.g. camera or photodetector) throughout exposure; no switching off, flicker or change in intensity is allowed.

requirements.text: The immunity of the ESA to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 16750-2 for the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b (Annex 10), with the levels of Tables 3a and 3b. The starting profile shall be assessed by the functional status classification of ISO 16750-1, and the pulses by the FPSC of ISO 7637-1.
requirements.test_case: Apply the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 pulses to the lamp supply input and classify the functional behaviour.

requirements.text: Where the ESA could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started by a 12 V/24 V starter motor, the ESA shall withstand the ISO 16750-2 starting profile at level II (12 V and 24 V systems), 10 pulses. Functional status shall be class B for immunity-related functions that must be operational during engine start, class C for other immunity-related functions, and class D for functions not related to immunity-related functions (e.g. reversing lamp).
requirements.test_case: Apply 10 level II starting-profile pulses per ISO 16750-2 and check the stop and rear position lamp behaviour against class B/C and the reversing lamp against class D.

requirements.text: The ESA shall withstand ISO 7637-2 pulse 1 at -75 V (12 V system) or -450 V (24 V system) for 500 pulses, with FPSC class III for both immunity-related and other functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply 500 pulses 1 at the applicable level and verify FPSC III for all lamp functions.

requirements.text: The ESA shall withstand ISO 7637-2 pulse 2a at +37 V (12 V and 24 V systems) for 500 pulses, with FPSC class I for immunity-related functions (stop lamp, rear position lamp) and class III for other functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply 500 pulses 2a at +37 V and verify that the stop and rear position lamps are unaffected (class I) and that the reversing lamp meets class III.

requirements.text: The ESA shall withstand ISO 7637-2 pulse 2b at +10 V (12 V system) or +20 V (24 V system) for 10 pulses, with FPSC class II for immunity-related functions and class III for other functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply 10 pulses 2b at the applicable level and verify class II for the stop and rear position lamps and class III for the reversing lamp.

requirements.text: The ESA shall withstand ISO 7637-2 pulse 3a at -112 V (12 V system) or -150 V (24 V system) for 1 h, with FPSC class I for immunity-related functions and class III for other functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply pulse 3a for 1 h at the applicable level and verify class I for the stop and rear position lamps and class III for the reversing lamp.

requirements.text: The ESA shall withstand ISO 7637-2 pulse 3b at +75 V (12 V system) or +150 V (24 V system) for 1 h, with FPSC class I for immunity-related functions and class III for other functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply pulse 3b for 1 h at the applicable level and verify class I for the stop and rear position lamps and class III for the reversing lamp.

requirements.text: In case the ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz (e.g. passive resistor/linear LED drive), it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.6.2 and Annex 8 (narrowband emission).
requirements.test_case: Review the schematic and bill of materials to confirm there is no oscillator, switching regulator, PWM or microcontroller clock above 9 kHz.

requirements.text: In case the ESA is not switched, contains no switches or does not include an inductive load, it need not be tested for transient conducted emission and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
requirements.test_case: Review the circuit design for internal switching elements and inductive loads to justify omitting the ISO 7637-2 emission test.

requirements.text: Rear lamps (ESAs) approved under UN R10 shall be manufactured so as to conform to the approved type by meeting the requirements of paragraph 6 (paragraph 7 does not apply, as the lamp has no REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid).
requirements.test_case: Audit production samples against the approved ESA specification and repeat the paragraph 6 emission and immunity tests on series parts.

requirements.text: When a series-production rear lamp (ESA) is verified for conformity, its measured broadband radiated emission levels shall not exceed the ESA broadband reference limits of paragraph 6.5.2.1 by more than 4 dB (60 per cent). These limits are 62 to 52 dBµV/m (30–75 MHz), 52 to 63 dBµV/m (75–400 MHz) and 63 dBµV/m (400–1,000 MHz).
requirements.test_case: Measure broadband radiated emissions of a production sample per Annex 7 and check that the levels are at or below the 6.5.2.1 limits + 4 dB.

requirements.text: When a series-production rear lamp (ESA) is verified for conformity, its measured narrowband radiated emission levels shall not exceed the ESA narrowband reference limits of paragraph 6.6.2.1 by more than 4 dB (60 per cent). These limits are 52 to 42 dBµV/m (30–75 MHz), 42 to 53 dBµV/m (75–400 MHz) and 53 dBµV/m (400–1,000 MHz).
requirements.test_case: Measure narrowband radiated emissions of a production sample per Annex 8 and check that the levels are at or below the 6.6.2.1 limits + 4 dB.

requirements.text: A series-production rear lamp (ESA) subjected to a radiated field strength of up to 80 per cent of the reference limits of paragraph 6.8.2.1 shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle that could be observed by the driver or other road users. This includes the stop lamp and rear position lamp functions.
requirements.test_case: Perform the Annex 9 radiated immunity test on a production sample at 80 % of the 6.8.2.1 field strength while monitoring the stop and rear position lamp outputs for any degradation.

requirements.text: A series-production rear lamp (component or STU) shall show no degradation of performance of its immunity-related functions (stop lamp, rear position lamp) when subjected to conducted transient disturbances on the 12/24 V supply lines up to the levels given in paragraph 6.9.1.
requirements.test_case: Apply the Annex 10 conducted transient pulses at the 6.9.1 levels to a production sample and monitor the stop and rear position lamp functions for degradation.

requirements.text: A series-production rear lamp (component or STU) shall not exceed the conducted transient emission levels given in paragraph 6.7.1 on its 12/24 V supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Measure conducted transient emissions of a production sample on the supply lines per Annex 10 and compare them with the 6.7.1 levels.

requirements.text: The broadband electromagnetic emissions of the rear lamp ESA (LED modules on PCB with driving circuitry) shall be measured according to CISPR 25, unless otherwise stated in Annex 7. This applies where the broadband emission test is not waived under the exceptions of paragraph 6.10, e.g. for a passive LED drive.
requirements.test_case: Perform the radiated broadband emission measurement on the lamp ESA per CISPR 25 and confirm that the test report references the Annex 7 method.

requirements.text: During the broadband emission test the rear lamp ESA shall be in normal operation mode, preferably at maximum load, i.e. with the rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions energised.
requirements.test_case: Check the test set-up and report to confirm that all lamp functions are energised in normal operation at maximum load during the scan.

requirements.text: For an ESA not involved in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid', such as this rear lamp, the broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25. As an alternative, an OATS complying with CISPR 16-1-4 may be used.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the emission test was carried out in an ALSE per CISPR 25 Clause 6.4, or in a compliant OATS.

requirements.text: The rear lamp ESA shall meet the broadband emission limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz when measured in an ALSE or OATS. The limits are 62 to 52 dBµV/m from 30 to 75 MHz (decreasing logarithmically), 52 to 63 dBµV/m from 75 to 400 MHz (increasing logarithmically) and a constant 63 dBµV/m from 400 to 1,000 MHz.
requirements.test_case: Scan 30–1,000 MHz in horizontal and vertical polarisation and compare the readings with the paragraph 6.5.2.1 limit line.

requirements.text: The broadband emission limits apply to quasi-peak detection. If peak detectors are used to measure the rear lamp ESA, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied before comparing the readings with the limits.
requirements.test_case: Check that peak readings were corrected by 20 dB, or that quasi-peak detection was used, before comparison with the limits.

requirements.text: For the rear lamp ESA, the maximum of the readings relative to the limit, over horizontal and vertical polarisation, in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.
requirements.test_case: Review the test data to confirm that the worst-case polarisation reading in each band is used as the characteristic value and lies below the limit.

requirements.text: The narrowband electromagnetic emission of the rear lamp ESA (LED modules on PCB with wiring/connector) shall be tested according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4 of CISPR 25. Any point not stated in Annex 8 follows CISPR 25. As an alternative, an OATS complying with CISPR 16-1-4 may be used.
requirements.test_case: Perform the narrowband radiated emission measurement in an ALSE per CISPR 25 clause 6.4 (or a CISPR 16-1-4 compliant OATS) and review the test report.

requirements.text: During the narrowband emission test, the rear lamp ESA shall be in normal operation mode, preferably at maximum load (e.g. rear position, stop and reversing functions energised at rated supply voltage).
requirements.test_case: Check the test set-up and log that all lamp functions are active at nominal 12 V/24 V supply, at maximum load, during the scan.

requirements.text: The narrowband emission limits for the rear lamp ESA shall be met throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.test_case: Scan from 30 to 1,000 MHz and compare the emissions against the 6.6.2.1 limit line over the full range.

requirements.text: Narrowband emissions of the rear lamp ESA shall be assessed with an average detector.
requirements.test_case: Verify in the test report that the narrowband emission results were measured with an average detector.

requirements.text: For the rear lamp ESA, the maximum of the readings relative to the limit, taken over horizontal and vertical antenna polarisation in each of the 14 frequency bands, shall be the characteristic reading at the measured frequency. This characteristic reading shall comply with the narrowband limit.
requirements.test_case: Measure in both horizontal and vertical polarisation and confirm that the worst-case reading in each band is below the limit.

requirements.text: For radiated immunity, the ESA (rear lamp) may comply with any combination of the following test methods, at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that together they cover the full frequency range of 20 to 6,000 MHz: absorber chamber test (ISO 11452-2), TEM cell test (ISO 11452-3), bulk current injection (ISO 11452-4), stripline test (ISO 11452-5) or reverberation chamber test (ISO 11452-11). Frequency range and general test conditions are based on ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Review the test plan and reports to confirm that the selected methods together cover 20–6,000 MHz without gaps.

requirements.text: The ESA immunity test conditions shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Check the test report for conformity of the test conditions (temperature, supply voltage, etc.) with ISO 11452-1.

requirements.text: During immunity testing, the ESA (rear lamp) shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition, i.e. with its stop lamp and rear position lamp functions active.
requirements.test_case: Verify during the test that the lamp is powered and its stop and rear position functions are activated and monitored.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be subjected to radiated immunity testing over the frequency range 20 to 6,000 MHz, with frequency step size and dwell time according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Perform the immunity sweep from 20 to 6,000 MHz with ISO 11452-1 steps and dwell times, and check the functions for deviations.

requirements.text: In the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, the immunity test signal shall be amplitude modulated (AM) with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, unless otherwise agreed between the Technical Service and the ESA manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Expose the lamp to AM 1 kHz / 80 % signals from 20 to 400 MHz and monitor lamp operation.

requirements.text: In the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, the immunity test signal shall be pulse modulated PM2 with Ton 3 µs and a period of 3,333 µs, unless otherwise agreed between the Technical Service and the ESA manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Expose the lamp to PM2 (3 µs on / 3,333 µs period) signals from 2,700 to 3,100 MHz and monitor lamp operation.

requirements.text: In the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, the immunity test signal shall be pulse modulated PM3 with Ton 500 µs and a period of 1,000 µs, unless otherwise agreed between the Technical Service and the ESA manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Expose the lamp to PM3 (500 µs on / 1,000 µs period) signals in 380–2,700 MHz and 3,100–6,000 MHz and monitor lamp operation.

requirements.text: In case the absorber chamber test is used, the ESA shall be exposed to antenna-generated radiation with the test field established by the substitution method according to ISO 11452-2 and with vertical polarization.
requirements.test_case: Perform the ISO 11452-2 absorber chamber test using vertical polarization and substitution-method field calibration.

requirements.text: In case TEM cell testing is used, the ESA shall be tested according to ISO 11452-3, with maximum field coupling to either the ESA or its wiring harness.
requirements.test_case: Perform the ISO 11452-3 TEM cell test in the maximum-coupling orientation chosen by the Technical Service.

requirements.text: In case bulk current injection is used, the ESA shall be tested according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench, either by the substitution method with the injection probe 150 mm from the ESA or by the closed loop method with the injection probe 900 mm from the ESA.
requirements.test_case: Perform ISO 11452-4 BCI on the lamp harness with the probe at 150 mm (substitution) or 900 mm (closed loop).

requirements.text: As an alternative to bench BCI, the ESA may be tested while installed in the vehicle according to ISO 11451-4, using the substitution method with the injection probe 150 mm from the ESA.
requirements.test_case: If chosen, perform in-vehicle BCI per ISO 11451-4 with the probe 150 mm from the lamp.

requirements.text: In case stripline testing is used, the ESA wiring harness shall be subjected to the specified field strengths according to ISO 11452-5.
requirements.test_case: Perform the ISO 11452-5 stripline test on the lamp harness.

requirements.text: In case the reverberation chamber test is used, the ESA shall be tested according to ISO 11452-11 using a test setup with ground plane, unless otherwise specified.
requirements.test_case: Perform the ISO 11452-11 reverberation chamber test with a ground-plane setup.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be subjected to test pulse 1 according to ISO 7637-2, applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines, as part of the immunity against transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulse 1 to the lamp supply and operationally connected inputs and check functional status against the immunity criteria of the regulation.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be subjected to test pulse 2a according to ISO 7637-2, applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulse 2a to the lamp supply and connected inputs and verify the lamp functions meet the required functional status.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be subjected to test pulse 2b according to ISO 7637-2, applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulse 2b to the lamp supply and connected inputs and verify the lamp functions meet the required functional status.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be subjected to test pulse 3a according to ISO 7637-2, applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulse 3a to the lamp supply and connected inputs and verify the stop and rear position lamp functions remain unaffected.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be subjected to test pulse 3b according to ISO 7637-2, applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulse 3b to the lamp supply and connected inputs and verify the stop and rear position lamp functions remain unaffected.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be subjected to the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2, applied to the supply lines and to other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile to the lamp supply and connected inputs and check the lamp's functional status during and after the profile.

requirements.text: In case the ESA is exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without 12 V/24 V starter motor), the ESA is not subject to the ISO 16750-2 starting profile test.
requirements.test_case: Check the manufacturer's declaration and the restrictions of use for exclusive EV fitment before omitting the starting profile test.

requirements.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines, and on other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines, shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2.
requirements.test_case: Measure switching transient emissions of the lamp on its supply lines per ISO 7637-2 and compare them with the permitted values.

requirements.text: The lamp shall have a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp drawing and sample to confirm there is a dedicated marking area large enough for all required markings.

requirements.text: All markings on the lamp shall be clearly legible and indelible.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the markings visually and perform a rub/durability check to confirm legibility and permanence.

requirements.text: The dimension "a" of the approval marking shall be at least 5 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure the dimension "a" of the moulded or printed approval mark on the lamp.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the approval mark: a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country that granted approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the circled E and the country number.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the four- to six-digit sequential number that forms part of the approval number.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the 4-6 digit sequential number and check it against the approval documentation.

requirements.text: The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking layout to confirm the sequential number sits adjacent to the circled E.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the approved lamp functions per paragraph 3.2.4: R1 (in case of steady rear position lamp) or R2 (in case of variable intensity rear position lamp); S1 (in case of steady stop lamp) or S2 (in case of variable intensity stop lamp); and AR for the reversing lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the function symbols and compare them with the approved functions and classes.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the number of the Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits of the series of amendments in force at the time of approval (e.g. 148R01).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for "148R" followed by the correct series-of-amendments digits.

requirements.text: In case the lamp cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, it shall bear a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
requirements.test_case: Check the design for side dependency and, if side-specific, inspect the marking for the horizontal arrow.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp (and rear end-outline marker lamp) function, the horizontal mounting arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the arrow orientation relative to the intended mounting side.

requirements.text: In case the reversing lamp has a reduced light distribution for fitment of two reversing lamps, the horizontal mounting arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: For the reduced-distribution variant, inspect that the arrow points outboard.

requirements.text: In case the lamp may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps, the additional letter "D" shall be placed to the right side of the function symbol.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for "D" to the right of the relevant function symbol.

requirements.text: In case the lamp is used as part of an interdependent lamp system, the additional letter "Y" shall be placed to the right side of the function symbol.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for "Y" to the right of the relevant function symbol.

requirements.text: In case the lamp (e.g. the reversing lamp) has a reduced light distribution per paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3, it shall bear a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
requirements.test_case: For the reduced-distribution variant, inspect the marking for the downward vertical arrow on a horizontal segment.

requirements.text: The lamp shall bear the approval marking.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the production sample for the presence of the complete approval marking.

requirements.text: The lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the applicant's trade name or mark.

requirements.text: In case of non-replaceable LED light sources, the lamp is exempted from the marking of the light source category or categories.
requirements.test_case: Confirm the light sources are non-replaceable and that no category marking is needed.

requirements.text: The lamp shall bear a marking of its rated voltage(s) (e.g. 12V) or voltage range, because it has non-replaceable light sources (and, where applicable, an electronic light source control gear, a variable luminous intensity control or a secondary operating mode).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the rated voltage or voltage range marking and compare it with the specification.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, each module shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect each module for the applicant's trade name or mark.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, each module shall bear its specific identification code: the letters "MD" followed by the approval mark without the circle, plus additional symbols or characters where several non-identical modules are used. The module and lamp approval marks shall be from the same applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module for the MD code format and check the applicant against the lamp approval.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, each module shall bear its rated voltage(s) or voltage range.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module for the rated voltage marking.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the MD identification code matching the module.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or voltage range.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the rated voltage marking.

requirements.text: In case an electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control is part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body, it shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the external control unit for its identification number and manufacturer name.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp that is not designed to be separated from the light-emitting transparent part of the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Review the assembly design to confirm the marked part cannot be separated from the outer lens.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle, or when a movable part such as the boot lid or a door is opened.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp installed on the vehicle (with the boot lid open if needed) to confirm the approval marking is visible.

requirements.text: If the outer lens is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
requirements.test_case: Check whether the lens is detachable and, if so, inspect both the lens and the housing for the approval marking.

requirements.text: In case the outer lens is used for several devices and bears different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the main body marking to confirm it lists only its own functions.

requirements.text: The approval marking, the trade name or mark, the rated voltage marking, the module identification code and voltage (for lamps with replaceable modules) and, where applicable, the external control gear identification shall be affixed on the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp assembly for the presence of all listed markings.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source modules are used, the module markings (trade name, MD identification code, rated voltage) shall be affixed on the module itself.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module component for its markings.

requirements.text: The trade name, light source category, rated voltage, light source module and control gear markings need not be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Confirm that only the approval marking is required to be visible when installed.

requirements.text: Where the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (R148 lamp functions and the R150 retro-reflector) comply with several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four- to six-digit sequential number may be affixed, located anywhere on the lamp assembly subject to paragraphs 3.3.5.1.1 and 3.3.5.1.2.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the single combined approval mark and its content against the approvals granted.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark is used, it shall be visible after installation of the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp installed on the vehicle for visibility of the single approval mark.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark is used, no light-transmitting part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Review the assembly design to confirm the lens and retro-reflector cannot be removed independently of the marked part.

requirements.text: The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the UN Regulations under which approval was granted (R148, R150).
requirements.test_case: Measure the mark component dimensions and compare them with the minimum sizes required by R148 and R150.

requirements.text: The general and individual specifications (sections 5 and 6 and referenced annexes) of UN R48 in force at the time of application shall apply to each lamp function for vehicle category M1, where their verification at lamp type approval is feasible.
requirements.test_case: Check the lamp against applicable R48 §5/§6 requirements, e.g. geometric visibility and colour, during approval testing.

requirements.text: The lamp shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which it may be subjected, its satisfactory operation remains assured and it retains the characteristics prescribed by R148.
requirements.test_case: Vibration test of the mounted lamp followed by functional and photometric re-check.

requirements.text: A lamp approved as a rear position lamp is deemed also to be approved as a rear end-outline marker lamp.
The rear position lamp, being grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp and reversing lamp, may also be used as an end-outline marker lamp.

In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with another function using a common light source and is designed to operate permanently with an additional intensity-regulating system, this arrangement is permitted.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the circuit design and verify the intensity regulation in both function modes.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, these functions shall either be provided by multiple light sources or be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure of the lamps.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the LED circuit for separate light sources per function, or verify the declared tell-tale failure-signal output.

requirements.text: In case a manufacturer logo is incorporated in the internal optical structure or outer lens texture within the apparent surface of the rear position lamp, only one logo may be incorporated, all requirements for the rear position lamp function shall still be fulfilled, and the logo shall be only that of the brand name of the vehicle or body manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the logo and the manufacturer statement, and repeat full photometry of the rear position lamp with the logo present.

requirements.text: In case a logo is incorporated, the enclosed light-emitting surface of the logo (transparent and non-transparent components) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.
requirements.test_case: Measure the projected logo light-emitting area in the reference axis direction.

requirements.text: Notwithstanding paragraph 5.5.2 of UN R48, the logo light-emitting surface does not have to be symmetrical by itself.
The stop lamp and the reversing lamp functions shall not incorporate a logo.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the apparent surfaces of the stop and reversing lamp functions for the absence of any logo.

requirements.text: In a lamp function containing more than one LED light source, a group of light sources wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.
requirements.test_case: Analyse the LED circuit topology (series strings) to identify the light-source groups for the failure analysis.

requirements.text: In case of failure of any one light source in a lamp function containing more than one light source (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp), either the light intensity shall still comply with the minimum intensities of the pertinent Annex 3 standard light distribution while the maximum intensities are not exceeded with all light sources lit, or a signal for activation of a failure tell-tale per R48 (e.g. 6.4.8, 6.7.8, 6.10.8) shall be produced.
requirements.test_case: Disable each LED group in turn and measure photometry against minimum values, or verify the tell-tale failure-signal output.

requirements.text: In case of a rear position lamp of category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, failure of the variable intensity control shall automatically result in fulfilment of the steady luminous intensity requirements of category R1.
requirements.test_case: Simulate a failure of the variable intensity control and measure that the intensities fall within the R1 limits.

requirements.text: In case of a stop lamp of category S2 emitting more than the maximum value of category S1, failure of the variable intensity control shall automatically result in fulfilment of the steady luminous intensity requirements of category S1.
requirements.test_case: Simulate a failure of the variable intensity control and measure that the intensities fall within the S1 limits.

requirements.text: The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light sources approved to UN R37, R99 and/or R128 (without use restriction), and/or light source modules, and/or non-replaceable light sources.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the light source design and documentation.

requirements.text: The lamp (light-signalling device) shall not generate radiated or power-line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: EMC emission tests (radiated and conducted) per R10 ESA methods.

requirements.text: In case of a replaceable light source module, the module shall only be fittable in the designated and correct position and shall only be removable with the use of tool(s).
requirements.test_case: Attempt incorrect fitment and tool-free removal of the module.

requirements.text: In case of a replaceable light source module, the module shall be tamperproof.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module design for tamper resistance.

requirements.text: In case of a replaceable light source module, regardless of the use of tools, the module shall not be interchangeable with any replaceable UN-approved light source or with any other replaceable light source module of different characteristics in the same lamp housing.
requirements.test_case: Attempt cross-fitting of other modules and UN-approved light sources into each module position.

requirements.text: In case of a replaceable light source module, when the module is replaced by another module from the applicant bearing the same identification code, the photometric requirements of the lamp shall be met.
requirements.test_case: Swap in a second module with the same MD code and repeat the photometric measurements.

requirements.text: Photometric and colorimetric compliance shall be achieved with the non-replaceable light sources or light source modules present in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Photometric and colorimetric measurement of the complete lamp with its own LEDs.

requirements.text: Where the lamp may be installed in more than one position or a field of positions, the photometric requirements shall be met in each position or at the extreme positions of the field of the reference axis specified by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Repeat photometry for each declared mounting position or the extreme positions.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, the luminous intensities shall be met with the light sources continuously lit.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensities with the LEDs continuously powered.

requirements.text: The intensity requirement for a particular direction of observation is deemed satisfied if it is met in a direction deviating by not more than one-quarter of a degree from that direction.
requirements.test_case: In case of challenge, check the intensity within ±0.25° of the test point.

requirements.text: For a 12 V system, the lamp functions shall meet the photometric requirements with 13.5 V supplied at the lamp, unless otherwise specified.
requirements.test_case: Supply 13.5 V at the lamp connector during photometric testing.

requirements.text: In case the lamp is intended for a 24 V system, the lamp functions shall meet the photometric requirements with 28 V supplied at the lamp, unless otherwise specified.
requirements.test_case: Supply 28 V at the lamp connector during photometric testing.

requirements.text: In case the lamp is controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall meet the requirements when operated as specified by the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp with the declared control gear and settings during testing.

requirements.text: In case the lamp with non-replaceable light sources or light source modules is not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control, the lamp shall meet the requirements when operated as specified by the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp at the applicant-declared supply conditions during testing.

requirements.text: The luminous intensity of each lamp function, on each of the two samples, shall on the reference axis (HV) be not less than the minimum specified in the pertinent table of paragraph 5 (Table 4 for R1/R2, stop lamp table for S1/S2, reversing lamp table for AR).
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement at HV for each function on both samples.

requirements.text: The luminous intensity of each lamp function shall in no direction where the lamp is visible exceed the maximum specified in the pertinent table of paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric scan of the full visible field for each function, compared with the maximum values.

requirements.text: Outside the reference axis, the luminous intensity of each lamp function shall be not less than the minimum of the pertinent paragraph 5 table multiplied by the percentage given in the pertinent Annex 3 light distribution figure (Figure A3-I for R and S), or not less than the absolute value given in that figure (Figure A3-V for AR).
requirements.test_case: Measure the Annex 3 grid points for each function and compare with the derived minima.

requirements.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Annex 2, the luminous intensity of each lamp function shall be not less than the minimum specified for geometric visibility in the pertinent table of paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity across the Annex 2 geometric visibility field for each function.

requirements.text: The provisions of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity shall be observed for each lamp function.
requirements.test_case: Check intermediate grid directions against the lowest surrounding minimum (50 % rule for AR).

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp or stop lamp is approved as an assembly of two independent lamps marked "D" deemed to be a single lamp, it shall comply with the maximum intensity requirement when all lamps together are lit.
requirements.test_case: Measure maximum intensities with both lamps of the assembly lit.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp or stop lamp is approved as an assembly of two independent lamps marked "D", it shall comply with the minimum intensity requirement if either lamp has failed.
requirements.test_case: Measure minimum intensities with each lamp of the assembly switched off in turn.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp or stop lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system marked "Y", the system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
requirements.test_case: Photometric and colorimetric test with all interdependent lamps operated together.

requirements.text: In case the interdependent rear position lamp system is partly mounted on a fixed and partly on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the outboard geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component, the inboard visibility being deemed satisfied if they still meet the photometric values of the light distribution field at those positions.
requirements.test_case: Photometric and visibility measurement at each fixed position of the movable component.

requirements.text: In case of a variable-intensity rear position lamp (R2) or stop lamp (S2), the variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensities over the full control range and compare with the paragraph 5 limits.

requirements.text: In case of a variable intensity control depending only on daytime and night-time conditions, it shall not cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady (R1/S1) maximum under night-time conditions.
requirements.test_case: Set the control to night-time mode and measure the maximum intensity against the R1/S1 maximum.

requirements.text: In case of other variable intensity control systems, the control shall not cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady (R1/S1) maximum under standard conditions (MOR > 2,000 m, clean lens).
requirements.test_case: Set the control to standard-condition inputs and measure the maximum intensity.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, the ratio between the intensities measured with both turned on simultaneously and with the rear position lamp alone should be at least 5:1 within ±5° V and ±10° H, with all light sources in operation where a function has several light sources considered as a single lamp.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensities with R alone and with R+S over the ±10° H / ±5° V field and compute the ratio at each point.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by each function (red for rear position and stop lamps, white for reversing lamp) shall meet the requirements when measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for that function in Annex 3, using the test procedure of paragraph 4.8.
requirements.test_case: Spectroradiometric chromaticity measurement at grid points for each function.

requirements.text: Outside the field of the light distribution grid, no sharp variation of the colour of light emitted by each function shall be observed.
requirements.test_case: Visual and colorimetric check of colour uniformity outside the grid field.

requirements.text: In case of a steady rear position lamp (R1): the minimum luminous intensity on the reference axis shall be 4 cd. The maximum luminous intensity in any direction where the lamp is visible shall be 17 cd for a single lamp, or 8.5 cd for a lamp marked "D". The standard light distribution shall follow Figure A3-I. The minimum intensity within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 shall be 0.05 cd.
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement of R1 samples at 13.5 V (or as specified) against the Table 4 R1 values.

requirements.text: In case of a variable intensity rear position lamp (R2): the minimum luminous intensity on the reference axis shall be 4 cd. The maximum luminous intensity in any direction where the lamp is visible shall be 42 cd for a single lamp, or 21 cd for a lamp marked "D". The standard light distribution shall follow Figure A3-I. The minimum intensity within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 shall be 0.05 cd.
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement of R2 samples over the full variable intensity range against the Table 4 R2 values.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, a luminous intensity of 60 cd is permitted for the rear position lamp below a plane forming an angle of 5° downward from the horizontal plane.
requirements.test_case: Measure rear position lamp intensity below 5°D and check that it is at most 60 cd where this relaxation is used.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall emit at least 0.05 cd within its angles of geometric visibility. These angles are 45° inboard and 80° outboard horizontally, reduced to 20° inboard below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm. Vertically they are 15° above and 15° below, reduced to 5° below for a mounting height of the H-plane below 750 mm.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer scan over the Table A2-1 angular field for R1/R2, checking for at least 0.05 cd at every direction.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the emitted light, checking the chromaticity coordinates against the red limits.

requirements.text: In case of a steady stop lamp (S1): the minimum luminous intensity on the reference axis shall be 60 cd. The maximum luminous intensity shall be 260 cd for a single lamp, or 130 cd for a lamp marked "D". The standard light distribution shall follow Figure A3-I. The minimum intensity within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 shall be 0.3 cd.
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement of S1 samples against the Table 7 S1 values.

requirements.text: In case of a variable intensity stop lamp (S2): the minimum luminous intensity on the reference axis shall be 60 cd. The maximum luminous intensity shall be 730 cd for a single lamp, or 365 cd for a lamp marked "D". The standard light distribution shall follow Figure A3-I. The minimum intensity within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 shall be 0.3 cd (day) and 0.07 cd (night).
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement of S2 samples in day and night modes against the Table 7 S2 values.

requirements.text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall meet the Table 7 minimum intensity within its angles of geometric visibility. These angles are 45° inboard and 45° outboard horizontally, reduced to 20° inboard below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm. Vertically they are 15° above and 15° below, reduced to 5° below for a mounting height of the H-plane below 750 mm.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer scan over the Table A2-1 stop lamp angular field, checking the 0.3 cd (S2 night: 0.07 cd) minimum.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the stop lamp light against the red chromaticity limits.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp (AR) shall have a minimum luminous intensity on the reference axis of 80 cd. It shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-V outside the reference axis.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity at HV and at the Figure A3-V points, checking each against its minimum.

requirements.text: The luminous intensity of the reversing lamp (AR) shall not exceed 300 cd in or above the H-plane. It shall not exceed 600 cd below the H-plane down to 5°D. It shall not exceed 8,000 cd below 5°D.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer scan of all visible directions, checking the maximum in each vertical zone.

requirements.text: In case the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices (reduced light distribution), the photometric intensity may be verified only up to 30° inwards, where at least 25 cd shall be satisfied. This condition shall be clearly explained in the application documents.
requirements.test_case: Measure the reversing lamp distribution up to 30° inboard and verify at least 25 cd there.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the reversing lamp light against the white chromaticity limits.

requirements.text: Rear position, stop and reversing lamps shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved under UN R148, including the photometric and colorimetric requirements of paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Take random production lamps and compare their construction, photometry and colour with the approved type documentation and paragraph 5 requirements.

requirements.text: In conformity of production testing, no measured photometric value of a production rear position lamp (R1/R2), stop lamp (S1/S2) or reversing lamp (AR) shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in UN R148.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensities of production lamps at the Annex 3 points per paragraph 4.8 and check that each value is within 20 % of the prescribed minimum and maximum values.

requirements.text: For the minimum luminous intensities required throughout the fields of geometric visibility (Annex 2) and the light distribution (Annex 3), the measured values of production lamps shall be at least the 20 per cent equivalents of Table 12: 7∙10^-1 cd → 5∙10^-1 cd; 6∙10^-1 cd → 4∙10^-1 cd; 3∙10^-1 cd → 2∙10^-1 cd; 7∙10^-2 cd → 5∙10^-2 cd; 5∙10^-2 cd → 3∙10^-2 cd. For example, the rear position lamp's 5∙10^-2 cd within the angles of geometric visibility becomes 3∙10^-2 cd.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of production samples at the geometric-visibility boundary directions, comparing each value with the Table 12 20 % equivalent value.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 80° outboard. These angles are shown for a lamp mounted on the right side of the vehicle and are mirrored for the left side.
requirements.test_case: Check by goniometric measurement or apparent-surface visibility analysis that the light-emitting surface is visible over 45° inboard to 80° outboard horizontally.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp (R1, R2) is to be mounted with its H-plane below 750 mm, the minimum horizontal inboard angle below the H-plane may be reduced to 20°, with the outboard angle remaining 80°.
requirements.test_case: Verify visibility below the H-plane over 20° inboard to 80° outboard for the declared low mounting height.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane.
requirements.test_case: Check by goniometric measurement that the light-emitting surface is visible from 15° above to 15° below the H-plane.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp (R1, R2) is to be installed with its H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility may be reduced to 15° above and 5° below.
requirements.test_case: Verify visibility from 15° above to 5° below the H-plane for the declared low mounting height.

requirements.text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 45° outboard. These angles are shown for a lamp mounted on the right side of the vehicle and are mirrored for the left side.
requirements.test_case: Check by goniometric measurement that the stop lamp light-emitting surface is visible over 45° inboard to 45° outboard horizontally.

requirements.text: In case the stop lamp (S1, S2) is to be mounted with its H-plane below 750 mm, the minimum horizontal inboard angle below the H-plane may be reduced to 20°, with the outboard angle remaining 45°.
requirements.test_case: Verify stop lamp visibility below the H-plane over 20° inboard to 45° outboard for the declared low mounting height.

requirements.text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane.
requirements.test_case: Check by goniometric measurement that the stop lamp is visible from 15° above to 15° below the H-plane.

requirements.text: In case the stop lamp (S1, S2) is to be installed with its H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility may be reduced to 15° above and 5° below.
requirements.test_case: Verify stop lamp visibility from 15° above to 5° below the H-plane for the declared low mounting height.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp and the stop lamp, the luminous intensity in each direction of measurement shall be at least the percentage given in the applicable standard light distribution figure of the minimum intensity required for that function, with the resulting values mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at each grid direction, compared with the percentage of the required minimum intensity rounded down to three significant digits.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) of 750 mm or less above the ground, its photometric intensity may be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: Check the declared mounting height and limit the downward photometric verification to 5° below H when the height is 750 mm or less.

requirements.text: In case the stop lamp (category S1 or S2) is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) of 750 mm or less above the ground, its photometric intensity may be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: Check the declared mounting height and limit the downward photometric verification to 5° below H when the height is 750 mm or less.

requirements.text: Within the field of light distribution shown as a grid, the luminous intensity of the rear position lamp and the stop lamp in each direction inside a part of the field bounded by grid lines shall be at least the lowest minimum percentage value shown on the grid lines surrounding that direction.
requirements.test_case: Scan intermediate directions between grid points goniophotometrically and confirm each intensity is at least the lowest surrounding grid minimum.

requirements.text: If visual examination of the reversing lamp reveals substantial local variations of intensity, no luminous intensity measured between two of the prescribed directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower of the two minimum intensities prescribed for those directions.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the reversing lamp beam, and where local variations appear, measure intensities between adjacent measuring points and compare them with 50 % of the lower prescribed minimum.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp (R1/R2) shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, i.e. in each direction of measurement at least the percentage given in Figure A3-I of the minimum intensity required in Table 4.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at all Figure A3-I points, compared with the percentage of the Table 4 minimum.

requirements.text: The stop lamp (S1 or S2) shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, i.e. in each direction of measurement at least the percentage given in Figure A3-I of the minimum intensity required in Table 7 (60 cd).
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at all Figure A3-I points, compared with the percentage of 60 cd.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall emit, in each measuring point of Figure A3-V (angles relative to the reference axis passing through the centre of reference), at least the minimum luminous intensity in cd given in Figure A3-V.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of the reversing lamp at each Figure A3-V point, compared with the minimum cd values.

requirements.text: Mass-produced rear combination lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions) shall differ from the approved type, from a mechanical and geometric standpoint, by no more than inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Dimensional inspection of random production lamps against the approved type drawings.

requirements.text: Any production lamp chosen at random shall meet the photometric performance requirements for each of its functions (rear position, stop, reversing) when tested according to paragraph 4.8, with the non-replaceable LED light sources or light source modules present in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of random production lamps at the Annex 3 points for each function and comparison with paragraph 5 and CoP limits.

requirements.text: Production lamps shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates (red for rear position and stop lamp, white for reversing lamp) when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.
requirements.test_case: Spectroradiometric colour measurement of random production lamps within the light distribution field of each function.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp (LED technology), the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure the reversing lamp intensity distribution after 1 min and 10 min of operation and compare it with the minimum and maximum values.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp (R1/R2) using LED technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure the rear position lamp intensities after 1 min and after 30 min (or at photometric stability) and check the minimum and maximum limits.

requirements.text: For the stop lamp (S1/S2) using LED technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure the stop lamp intensities after 1 min and after 30 min (or at photometric stability) and check the minimum and maximum limits.

requirements.text: In addition to the checks of paragraph 1, the luminous intensity distribution of each lamp function shall comply at the point in time after switch ON listed in Table A8-1 for that function, depending on the light source technology.
requirements.test_case: Check the intensity distribution at the Table A8-1 time after switch ON, or confirm the deemed-compliance condition for LED-only functions.

requirements.text: Rear position lamp (also deemed end-outline marker lamp): the intensity requirements shall be met 4 s after switch ON, with HV as reference coordinate.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity at HV 4 s after switch ON and scale the distribution to verify compliance.

requirements.text: Stop lamp: the intensity requirements shall be met 0.2 s after switch ON, with HV as reference coordinate.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity at HV 0.2 s after switch ON with a fast photometer and verify compliance.

requirements.text: Reversing lamp: the intensity requirements shall be met 0.2 s after switch ON, with HV as reference coordinate.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity at HV 0.2 s after switch ON and verify compliance.

requirements.text: Where a lamp function uses LED technology only, the lamp function is deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2 are compliant.
requirements.test_case: Confirm that each function uses LED technology only and that the paragraph 1.2 measurements comply.

requirements.text: In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the minimum intensity requirements of each lamp function shall be met at all points in time, from the point in time listed in Table A8-1 until photometric stability is reached.
requirements.test_case: Record the intensity at the reference coordinate continuously from the Table A8-1 time until photometric stability and verify the minimum is never undercut.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall have a space large enough for either the Unique Identifier and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2, or the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the drawing and a sample to confirm there is a marking area large enough for the UI or the approval marking plus the other markings.

requirements.text: All markings on the retro-reflector shall be clearly legible and indelible.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the markings and rub them with water- and petrol-soaked cloths to check they stay legible.

requirements.text: The size of the approval marking shall be based on the value of 'a' defined in Table 1.
requirements.test_case: Measure the dimension 'a' of the approval marking on the sample.

requirements.text: For a retro-reflector for motor vehicles of Class IA (independent) or Class IB (combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight), the minimum 'a' of the approval marking is 5 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure 'a' on the approval mark and check it is at least 5 mm.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall contain the approval mark: a circle surrounding the letter 'E', followed by the distinguishing number of the country that granted approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the circled 'E' and the country number.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall contain the four- to six-digit sequential number that forms part of the approval number.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the sequential number and check it against the approval communication.

requirements.text: The sequential number of the approval number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking to confirm the sequential number sits next to the circled E.

requirements.text: In case the lamp containing the retro-reflector is watertight, the approval marking shall contain the class symbol 'IA' (retro-reflector for motor vehicles, independent).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the symbol 'IA'.

requirements.text: In case the lamp containing the retro-reflector is not watertight, the approval marking shall contain the class symbol 'IB' (retro-reflector for motor vehicles combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the symbol 'IB'.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall contain the Regulation number '150', followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits of the series of amendments in force when the approval was issued (e.g. 150R01).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for '150R' followed by the series digits.

requirements.text: The approval marking may be replaced by the Unique Identifier, if available; in that case the UI mark shall follow the format shown in Figure I.
requirements.test_case: If a UI is used, compare the marked UI with the Figure I format and check the database entry.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the sample for the applicant's trade name or mark.

requirements.text: A Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall bear the word 'TOP' written horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if this is needed to determine without ambiguity the angle(s) of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Check whether the photometry depends on rotation and, if so, inspect for 'TOP' on the uppermost part of the illuminating surface.

requirements.text: The approval marking or Unique Identifier, and the markings of paragraph 3.3.4, shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the sample to confirm all markings are legible on the device.

requirements.text: Where the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamps with the retro-reflector) comply with several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four- to six-digit sequential number, or a single Unique Identifier, may be affixed anywhere on the lamp assembly, subject to the conditions of paragraphs 3.3.6.1.1 and 3.3.6.1.2.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the single mark on the assembly and check that it covers all applicable approvals.

requirements.text: If a single approval mark or UI is used on the grouped/combined/reciprocally incorporated lamps, it shall be visible after the lamp is installed on the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp installed on the vehicle, or a mock-up, to confirm the mark is visible.

requirements.text: If a single approval mark or UI is used, no light-transmitting part of the grouped/combined/reciprocally incorporated lamps (e.g. the outer lens or the retro-reflector) shall be removable without also removing the approval mark with its sequential number or the UI.
requirements.test_case: Review the design and do a disassembly check that the mark sits on a part that cannot be separated from the light-transmitting parts.

requirements.text: The components of a single approval mark shall be no smaller than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the UN Regulations under which approval was granted (R150, R148).
requirements.test_case: Measure the mark components and compare them with the minimum sizes required by R150 and R148.

requirements.text: The requirements in sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications', and in the Annexes they reference, of UN Regulation No. 48 (series of amendments in force at the time of application) that are pertinent to the red rear retro-reflector and to vehicle category M1 shall be met, where their verification at the time of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
requirements.test_case: Review the R48 general and individual specifications for rear retro-reflectors on M1 vehicles and check the device for the items that can be verified at device level.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall be so constructed that it functions satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
requirements.test_case: Confirm that the retro-reflector meets its photometric requirements before and after the prescribed resistance tests.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector must not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to its efficient operation or to its maintenance in good condition.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the samples for design or manufacturing defects such as voids, sink marks or damaged prisms.

requirements.text: The components of the retro-reflector, or parts thereof, shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to dismantle the retro-reflector components by hand without tools and confirm they cannot easily be separated.

requirements.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall be easy to clean.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the outer surface and confirm by a cleaning trial that it can be cleaned easily.

requirements.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall not be rough, and any protuberances it may exhibit shall not prevent easy cleaning.
requirements.test_case: Visually and tactilely inspect the outer surface for roughness and for protuberances that hinder cleaning.

requirements.text: There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflector when in normal use.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the assembled lamp and confirm that the inner prism surface cannot be reached without dismantling.

requirements.text: In case the retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter (e.g. a colourless optical unit behind the red outer lens acting as filter), the optical unit and filter shall be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
requirements.test_case: Check by inspection and handling of the assembly that the optical unit and the filter cannot be separated in normal use.

requirements.text: The retro-reflecting optical unit and any filter shall not be coloured by means of paint or varnish.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the material, check the drawings and examine a cross-section to confirm that the red colour is integral to the material and not a paint or varnish layer.
